name: Buehler molecular-DFT multi-agent demonstration
demonstrated_target: finite organic molecules CCCCXCC, with X = C, O or N
boundary_conditions: molecular-coordinate DFT calculations; boundary conditions not independently resolved

sources.locator: Section 2.3.1 Molecular Design; Table 8; Materials and Methods
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Planner, coordinate-retriever and execution-capable chatbot agents devise a plan, obtain molecular coordinates from SMILES, call a supplied DFT function for the three molecular variants, analyze computed energies and answer the user.
The preprint introduces multi-agent code generation and execution connected to DFT-derived physical data; its first submission predates the 2024 journal publication.

aliases: Generative Retrieval-Augmented Ontologic Graph and Multiagent Strategies for Interpretive Large Language Model-Based Materials Design
limitations: Unnamed, small worked demonstration rather than a separately branded general-purpose package. Counting demonstrates agent-run DFT, not scientific validity of ranking absolute energies of molecules with different compositions. The MechGPT/RAG question-answering demonstrations in the same paper are not separately counted.

name: ProtAgents
demonstrated_target: PDB and de novo proteins; coarse-grained protein elastic networks
boundary_conditions: Finite protein structures represented by anisotropic spring networks; no periodic-cell example is inferred

sources.locator: Results §2.1–2.3 and Fig.3; Materials and Methods, Natural vibrational frequency calculations
sources.evidence_paraphrase: GPT-4 agents plan and invoke protein generation/folding and physics calculations; examples execute ProDy anisotropic-network normal-mode calculations on retrieved and generated structures. Chroma and OmegaFold generate the protein geometries.
The primary submission record dates the first version to 27 January 2024.

limitations: F denotes an actual coarse-grained elastic-network vibration calculation, not quantum-chemical molecular frequencies or ideal-gas thermochemistry. No D mark: MD is mentioned as an extensible capability and used in training another predictor, rather than demonstrated as an agent-run dynamics task.

name: LLaMP
demonstrated_target: Si crystal/interstitial and crystal annealing MD
boundary_conditions: crystalline supercells demonstrated; PBC not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Fetches a crystal, constructs a supercell, runs temperature-cycling ML-potential MD and analyzes its trajectory.

name: ChemReasoner
demonstrated_target: heterogeneous catalyst slabs and adsorbates
boundary_conditions: slab cells and vacuum explicitly reported

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM-guided catalyst search uses GNN structure relaxation and adsorption-energy feedback; selected slabs are checked by DFT.

name: AtomAgents
demonstrated_target: metallic alloys, dislocations and fracture
boundary_conditions: explicit periodic boundaries; dislocation cells also have a free direction

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Runs alloy property calculations, atomic relaxation and dislocation NEB; material-property experiments link simulation feedback to alloy hypotheses.

name: Adsorb-Agent
demonstrated_target: adsorbates on crystalline catalyst slabs
boundary_conditions: bulk-derived Miller-index slabs; explicit PBC not independently checked

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM proposes adsorption sites and orientations, with relaxed atomistic adsorption-energy evaluation. Bulk IDs and slab Miller indices are documented.

name: LangSim

boundary_conditions: crystal cells and energy–volume curves; explicit periodic-boundary flag not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Project authors describe an LLM calling ASE/EMT or MACE workflows that construct a crystal, optimize its geometry, and evaluate energy versus volume to obtain the bulk modulus.

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Official institute page reports successful agent-run Al calculations and iterative Cu–Au composition evaluation against a target bulk modulus.

limitations: Date is the earliest dated primary report inspected here, not a verified software launch date; the official page identifies a 2024 hackathon. The later 34 Examples report is the same project and is not counted again.

name: MDCrow
demonstrated_target: proteins and common solvents
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article; do not assume isolated molecules

demonstrated_target: LAMMPS materials thermodynamics
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Generates, executes and reviews LAMMPS simulation code for material thermodynamic tasks.

limitations: Semi-automated: the paper explicitly retains human involvement. It is included because the scope includes LLM modification/execution, not only fully autonomous agents.

name: El Agente Q
demonstrated_target: organic molecules and coordination complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular calculations (ORCA/xTB)

sources.locator: Abstract; corroborated by ChemGraph Discussion and Quntur Introduction

name: Aitomia

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Demonstrated examples include hexanol IR and multi-species reaction enthalpy workflows using geometry optimization, frequency and electronic calculations.

name: MatAgent (Lv et al.)
demonstrated_target: water octamer, (H2O)8, total energy and maximum force
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cluster is the concrete worked target; PWDFT is a plane-wave engine, but boundary conditions for this cluster are not established by the article

sources.evidence_paraphrase: GPT-4 chooses tools, supplies inputs and evaluates returned results. The structure tool supplies geometry and a PWDFT API executes first-principles energy/force calculations. The specific worked example asks for total energy and maximum force of a water octamer.

aliases: Bridging language models and computational materials science: A prompt-driven framework for material property prediction
limitations: The article's materials terminology and Materials Project interface are broader than its concrete demonstrated water-cluster case. Do not label its physical target extended materials solely because it uses PWDFT; no MD mark is inferred from a general AIMD equation or cited PWDFT work. Distinct from other systems also called MatAgent.

name: ChemGraph
demonstrated_target: PubChem small molecules and reaction thermochemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular benchmarks; ASE supports PBC but support is not counted as a demonstration

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Thirteen molecular tasks include DFT optimization, vibrations and reaction enthalpy/Gibbs calculations; no periodic benchmark is inferred from ASE support.

name: TopoMAS
demonstrated_target: SrSbO3 and Sr2Sb2O7 crystal generation; SrSbO3 topological classification
boundary_conditions: crystallographic space-group-constrained structures and VASP k-point files; periodic crystal workflow

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents invoke CrystalFormer for crystal generation, plan and submit VASP calculations through an HPC API, inspect outputs, recover an intentionally corrupted completion check, and compute topological invariants with SymTopo.

limitations: Interactive human–AI framework; benchmark QA results do not determine simulation task marks. Journal and preprint are one system.

name: NAMD-Agent
demonstrated_target: proteins in explicit solvent and lipid membranes, including 1UBQ, 1L2Y and membrane-builder examples
boundary_conditions: Explicit periodic boundary conditions in the solution and membrane examples (SI §§6.1–6.6)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Gemini composes, executes and revises code to operate CHARMM-GUI, assemble solvated protein or membrane systems, run NAMD, and analyze actual 1 ns trajectories. Example simulation parameters explicitly enable periodic boundaries.

aliases: Automating MD simulations for Proteins using Large language Models: NAMD-Agent
limitations: The inspected evidence is v1. T and D are positively coded; control over minimization settings alone is not used to infer a separate demonstrated O task. Protein or membrane boxes remain in the soft/biomolecular class despite PBC.

name: DREAMS
demonstrated_target: Sol27LC crystals and CO/Pt(111)
boundary_conditions: periodic crystal/lattice-constant and crystalline slab models

sources.locator: Main text; Sol27LC and CO/Pt(111) challenges
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Executes lattice-constant and adsorption-energy studies with DFT workflows and provenance checking.

name: SparksMatter
demonstrated_target: inorganic thermoelectrics, semiconductors and perovskite oxides
boundary_conditions: CIF crystal structures and periodic inorganic-material models; individual PBC flags not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: A coder agent invokes MatterGen for structures and a MatterSim-based evaluation module for atomistic relaxation and formation-energy convex-hull construction. Case studies use this feedback for inorganic-material candidate design.

limitations: Included because actual atomistic force-field relaxation is executed, not because CGCNN predicts properties. Follow-up DFT and synthesis recommendations in the report are not counted as agent-executed DFT.

name: AutoSolvate-Agent
demonstrated_target: water IR; molecular orbital, bond-order and charge analyses; benzaldehyde in implicit solvent; coordination complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular TeraChem calculations; PCM solvent in the benzaldehyde example

sources.locator: Sections 4.1 Frequency Analysis and 4.2 Solvatochromism Prediction; Figures 2–3; Appendix A.2 Table 1
sources.evidence_paraphrase: For water IR, the agent retrieves a geometry, interprets TeraChem's large-gradient frequency failure, inserts and completes a geometry optimization, and reruns frequency analysis. For benzaldehyde it sets up and executes PCM quantum chemistry and directs Multiwfn orbital-population analysis.
Ten evaluated problems include water IR and optimization, methane orbital energies, coordination-bond analyses, liquid-phase water dipole and cis/trans-2-butene energy differences.

sources.locator: Author Fangning Ren's Publications entry for AutoSolvate-Agent
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The author's publication entry dates the workshop contribution to 8 June 2025; the paper itself prints the KDD workshop date of 6 August 2025.

aliases: AutoSolvate-Agent: An Autonomous Agent for GPU-accelerated Solution-phase Quantum Chemistry
limitations: The dated field uses 6 August 2025 printed on the original workshop paper. An author publication list gives 8 June; exact OpenReview first-posting time remains unresolved. Original PDF text was inspected via its index while direct OpenReview opening encountered a browser challenge. This LLM workflow is distinct from intent-based AutoSolvateWeb. Solvatochromism is qualitatively inferred from orbitals, not an excited-state dynamics calculation.
date_basis: dated original KDD workshop paper; exact first posting unresolved

name: VASPilot
demonstrated_target: crystalline solids and transition-metal dichalcogenides
boundary_conditions: band structure/Brillouin-zone crystalline models

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Demonstrates band structures, density of states, cutoff convergence, lattice-constant optimization and band-gap comparisons.

name: ChemAgents molecular simulation workflow
demonstrated_target: bridged azobenzenes and azobenzene ground-state conformers and IR/Raman spectra
boundary_conditions: molecular AIMD/DFT examples; gas and solvent spectral data; explicit simulation boundaries not independently audited

sources.locator: Abstract; Figure 1; Results and discussion / Computation–experimentation integration and automated workflow execution; Conclusions
sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents formulate the study plan and coordinate automated computations. The Computation Performer runs ground-state AIMD conformer sampling and DFT IR/Raman calculations; the paper explicitly separates these from human-designed and trained neural-network analysis.
The original preprint describes the ChemAgents-orchestrated computational/experimental workflow and supplies its first-public date.

aliases: Unlocking azobenzene isomerization mechanisms via an LLM agent-driven workflow integrating simulation, experiment, and machine learning
limitations: The system's molecular-computation demonstration is counted once, rather than counting the accompanying robotic experiment or spectral prediction model as additional systems. Ground-state sampling and steady-state spectra do not demonstrate nonadiabatic photoisomerization dynamics or validated transition-state/IRC searches. Earlier ChemAgents platform work may establish an earlier family release, but this is the first verified atomistic demonstration located in this screening.

name: AMLP
demonstrated_target: acridine molecular-crystal polymorphs
boundary_conditions: monoclinic crystal cells, cell optimization and crystal AIMD; molecular identity does not make the demonstrated crystal an isolated molecule

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents assist electronic-structure code and parameter selection, input construction and conversion in a pipeline that performs DFT geometry/cell optimization and AIMD, trains a MACE potential and validates it with relaxation and NVE/NVT dynamics on acridine crystals.

limitations: LLM assistance sits within a substantially scripted pipeline. Article revisions and the JCTC counterpart are one system. MLIP development itself is not a new seventh task code.

name: ToPolyAgent
demonstrated_target: coarse-grained bead-spring linear, ring, brush, star and dendrimer polymers with solvent
boundary_conditions: Polymer–solvent simulation boxes are explicit; PBC is not separately resolved from the inspected article

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents invoke polymer/solvent construction and LAMMPS simulation tools. Brush and star examples execute dynamics, and interactive feedback changes grafting density or extends a simulation; research examples compare solvent interactions and polymer conformation.

sources.locator: Primary arXiv record and submission history
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The first report is dated 14 October 2025; the RSC journal title adds bead-spring but describes the same system.

aliases: ToPolyAgent: AI agents for coarse-grained bead-spring topological polymer simulations
limitations: Coarse-grained rather than all-atom MD. Interactive and autonomous modes are both included. The article HTML has a later rendering timestamp despite retaining the v1 identifier; date uses the primary submission record. Conformational/transport observables are coded under D, not F.

name: GENIUS
demonstrated_target: MC2D/MC3D materials; PdS2 geometry-relaxation example
boundary_conditions: 2D/3D crystal database targets; PdS2 example has a 7×7×2 k-point mesh

sources.locator: Prompt Dataset; Automated Error Handling; Results/Figs.6–7
sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLMs generate Quantum ESPRESSO input and repair failed executions using a parameter knowledge graph. The benchmark contains structural relaxation and single-shot DFT tasks; the worked PdS2 case generates BFGS relaxation input and shows an execution/recovery timeline.
The journal version describes its benchmark outcome as passing early execution validation, which is narrower than a verified converged physical result.

limitations: Task marks denote executed calculation types, not scientific completion. The preprint's run-to-completion wording must not overwrite the journal's early-execution-validation qualification. Geometry retrieval/standardization alone was not assigned an additional construction mark.

name: LAMMPS-Agents
demonstrated_target: elemental metals and binary alloys, including gold and Cu–Au
boundary_conditions: crystal models; exact PBC flags not independently audited from the inspected repository

sources.locator: README; lammps_agents.py demonstration prompts and simulation workflow

sources.locator: Introduction; Results static/dynamic property examples; Conclusion
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Authors report executed crystal construction, lattice/cohesive-energy and elastic-property calculations, structure relaxation, Phonopy phonon dispersion and melting-point MD for elemental and alloy targets.
Author institution identifies the paper and its 9 December 2025 publication date.

aliases: Multi-agentic AI framework for end-to-end atomistic simulations
limitations: The publisher's full text was available as a cached primary search response but direct opens returned 403; official repository and source were also inspected. Distinct from both DynaMate systems, AtomAgents and URSA. No soft-matter mark is inferred from future extensibility.

sources.locator: Title, author list and abstract of SimBioChem 2025 workshop counterpart

limitations: The dated field uses the verified arXiv date; an earlier DynAgent workshop version is identified but its posting date is unresolved, so this is not a secure earliest-appearance claim. This is unrelated to the LAMMPS/Moltemplate DynaMate of de Gillis et al. Endpoint MM/PBSA analysis is included under D, without E/F marks.

boundary_conditions: POSCAR crystal cells, supercells and heterostructures; explicit PBC flag not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The agent runs ALIGNN-FF iterative relaxation for an arbitrary TiAu structure. Its semiconductor-defect workflow constructs a supercell, substitutes atoms, optimizes the same structure and calculates a tight-binding band structure.

limitations: Database retrieval and scalar predictor calls alone are not the inclusion basis. No MD or protein-simulation mark is inferred from the platform's tool list. Journal and preprint count once.

sources.locator: Computational methods; Fig.2; Supplementary geometry tips

boundary_conditions: VASP periodic bulk and surface cells; surface k-point meshes explicitly reported

An Agentic Framework for Autonomous First-principles Calculations

Autonomous Computational Catalysis Research via Agentic Systems

A Universal Autonomous System for Atomistic Simulation and a Benchmark of Its Capabilities

demonstrated_target: molecules, organometallic complexes and TS-like geometries
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cases; slabs/solids are future extensions in inspected v1

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Invokes xTB constrained optimization to create intended molecular geometry; agentic geometric operations are real. Subsequent independent DFT TS checks are not coded as agent TS execution.

name: El Agente Quntur
demonstrated_target: molecular and coordination quantum chemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cases including isocyanide and acetylacetone

sources.locator: Results/case studies; Discussion/Geometric reasoning; Appendix B
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Demonstrates electronic methods, optimization/frequencies and reaction-path cases; isocyanide mechanistic refinement includes TS correction. NEB geometry failures are discussed, so this is task coverage rather than blanket success.

name: El Agente Gráfico
demonstrated_target: finite-molecule quantum chemistry and explicit microsolvation ensembles; metal-organic frameworks
boundary_conditions: finite molecular gas/implicit-solvent/15-water-cluster examples; separate MOF crystal/CIF construction and MLIP relaxation

sources.locator: Sections 2.1–2.3; Figure 3; Appendix C; Appendix D.1.7
sources.evidence_paraphrase: An LLM routing agent orchestrates typed single-point, optimization, frequency and TDDFT nodes. Molecular examples generate CREST conformers and a 15-water microsolvation cluster, optimize them, check imaginary modes and calculate ensemble spectra. A separate demonstrated MOF workflow constructs CIF structures, relaxes them with MACE and analyzes porosity.

sources.locator: Version 2 front matter, abstract, Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix E
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The updated semantic-execution-runtime report retains typed operations and frequency-based intermediate checks, and additionally reports open-ended disulfide redox-mechanism studies. Its expanded claims are distinguished from the v1 task-coding basis.

aliases: El Agente Gráfico: Structured Execution Graphs for Scientific Agents
limitations: Same research family as Q/Quntur/Estructural but a separately described execution-graph system, so not deduplicated merely by family. Cross-domain classification reflects actual finite molecular and MOF demonstrations. Its molecular imaginary-frequency failure recovery is not evidence of TS/IRC execution. The present matrix retains the inspected v1 task basis. Version 2 (7 August) has a revised title/author list and reports disulfide redox-mechanism work; the blank R cell is not a claim that the current system has no mechanistic applications. The polishing manuscript cites v2.

name: El Agente Sólido
demonstrated_target: crystals, Pt(111) oxygenated adsorbates, NMC-811, MOFs/COFs

aliases: El Agente Solido: A New Age(nt) for Solid State Simulations
limitations: Separate architecture/tool composition and benchmark from Q, Quntur, Estructural and Forjador, with family-level merge available. OER free-energy diagrams are not a transition-path/TS search, so no R is assigned from them.

CHELATRON: AI-Driven Molecular Discovery for Cancer Treatment

sources.locator: Sections II.1–II.2; Table S1 Chemistry and Molecular Science (GROMACS, LAMMPS, Psi4, PySCF); Table S2 CP2K
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Codex-driven workflows rerun molecular electronic-structure and molecular-dynamics packages. The paper distinguishes newly executed simulations from merely replotted figures; only executed cases support these marks.

limitations: General scientific infrastructure; non-atomistic physics and engineering tasks are not counted as chemistry evidence. Replotted and blocked tasks are not simulation successes. T/O/F/R remain unencoded without case-level evidence in this pass.

name: MatClaw
demonstrated_target: monolayer CuInP2S6 ferroelectric MD, potential distillation and domain-wall dynamics
boundary_conditions: 2D material and MD supercell targets; explicit PBC flags not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The code-writing LLM runs active-learning force-field distillation, atomistic energy/force evaluation, Curie-temperature MD and a field/temperature search for domain-wall propagation. Demonstrations discuss failed sampling/equilibration choices and researcher interventions.

aliases: An Autonomous Code-First LLM Agent for End-to-End Materials Exploration
limitations: Guided autonomy: high-level expert constraints and literature self-learning assist the agent. Do not count the March2026 APS presentation on the same CuInP2S6 agent as a second system; exact identity of that early abstract is retained in screening.

name: El Agente Forjador
demonstrated_target: molecular QC plus quantum dynamics
boundary_conditions: finite molecular examples; quantum-state dynamics does not imply periodic materials

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Creates and reuses tools for molecular optimization, frequencies/thermochemistry and excited states; hybrid cases couple electronic structure to quantum dynamics.

limitations: D is quantum dynamics, not necessarily atomistic MD. The physical target is coded by demonstrated molecular calculations, not software breadth.

name: MDAgent (biomolecular, 2026)
demonstrated_target: soluble and membrane proteins, protein–DNA/ligand systems and TMEM16F/XKR8 scramblase dynamics
boundary_conditions: Three-dimensional PBC for all simulated systems; explicit aqueous or lipid environments (Methods §4.5)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The LLM multi-agent system connects research planning to GROMACS system construction, steepest-descent minimization, equilibration and production. Demonstrations include membrane-protein dynamics and enhanced sampling; methods specify 3D periodic systems.

sources.locator: Primary record, title/authors and first submission
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The Ma/Yang/Song/Jiang biomolecular framework was first reported on 18 April 2026.

aliases: MDAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for End-to-End Molecular Dynamics Research
limitations: Distinct from the 2025 materials LAMMPS MDAgent. Umbrella-sampling PMF, metadynamics and SMD transport analyses remain D; no E/F/R mark is inferred from statistical free energies or transport paths. Some evaluation dimensions concern plans/reports, so task coding relies on the separately described executed simulation cases, not review scores.

name: VirtualLab_CC
demonstrated_target: stabilized Criegee intermediates and biogenic terpenes; molecular conformers, thermochemistry and PES study
boundary_conditions: finite molecular Gaussian/ORCA calculations with CREST/xTB conformer search

sources.locator: Section 2.1 and Table 1; prototype Criegee case study; Section 5.3; Section 6 Limitations
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Claude coordinates method proposals, task decomposition and failure interpretation around executed CREST conformer, DFT optimization/frequency and coupled-cluster jobs. The molecular campaign includes real production outputs and automatic repair of cluster-invocation failures, with human approvals for scientific decisions.

sources.locator: README / Architecture; HPC Integration; Method Protocols; release v1.1.0
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The official release documents its skill-driven LLM coordination, Gaussian/ORCA/CREST execution, result extraction and the Criegee–terpene case-study protocol.
Original preprint counterpart of the journal article; used to deduplicate the publication family and identify first appearance.

aliases: VirtualLab_CC: An LLM-Augmented Virtual Laboratory for Automated Computational Chemistry Research
limitations: The paper explicitly says transition-state location remains semi-manual and no automated reaction-discovery engine is included. Path/TS task R is therefore conservatively left uncoded here. Human approval at critical scientific decisions does not exclude demonstrated LLM planning, invocation and repair. Journal text was inspected through the indexed publisher original; direct opening returned HTTP 403.

name: XDFT
demonstrated_target: correlated and structurally complex crystalline metal/semiconductor mismatches
boundary_conditions: VASP crystal/supercell calculations with k-point density; defect, strain and polymorph interventions

sources.locator: Architecture pp.2–3; Methods p.10, Hypothesis library/First-principles/Bayesian hypothesis selection
sources.evidence_paraphrase: For each material an LLM advisor contributes a per-material hypothesis score to a Bayesian selector. The selected intervention modifies crystal structures or VASP inputs and executes first-principles tests; the resulting verdict updates the selector's state.

aliases: A self-evolving agent for explainable diagnosis of DFT–experiment band-gap mismatch
Discovering physical mechanisms from experiment–simulation mismatches
limitations: The LLM is not the entire selector: v1 explicitly weights the advisor score 0.2. Include because the LLM influences actual per-material computational choices. Later revisions change the benchmark and title; do not mix their result counts. R is chemical/structural paths, not diagnostic mechanism attribution, so none is assigned.

name: TSAgent
demonstrated_target: heterogeneous catalytic reactions on slabs
boundary_conditions: VASP slab geometry; 2×2×1 k-point grid explicitly reported

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Adapts geometry optimization, NEB and vibrational TS verification on OC20NEB surface-reaction cases.

name: Lang2MLIP
demonstrated_target: graphite/Li2CO3/LEDC/liquid-electrolyte multilayer solid-electrolyte interphase
boundary_conditions: solid, amorphous and liquid component cells and interfaces; explicit PBC flags not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Agents construct 60 component/interface configurations and an LLM decision-maker adaptively chooses reference calculations, MD sampling, training and evaluation. The demonstrated reference is the PFP interatomic potential, not DFT.

aliases: End-to-End Language-to-Machine Learning Interatomic Potential Development with Autonomous Agentic Workflows
limitations: Target coding follows the integrated solid–electrolyte interface study. Generic support for polymers, isolated clusters and other structure classes does not establish separate demonstrated research domains. No DFT-execution claim is inferred from interchangeable reference backends.

name: AtomisticSkills
demonstrated_target: solid electrolytes, MOFs, catalyst surfaces and protein–ligand complexes
boundary_conditions: crystal and surface cells plus explicit-water biomolecular MD; not a single PBC class

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Coding agents construct and relax solids, submit DFT energies/forces, sample configurations by MD, and execute explicit-water MD refinement of docked protein–ligand complexes.

limitations: A skills/tool harness for general coding agents. Human review of campaign plans is retained. Drug docking alone does not establish inclusion; the executed downstream MD does. MD-derived binding free energies are under D, not vibrational F.

name: ChatMOSP
demonstrated_target: Pd and Pt catalytic nanoparticles under CO oxidation
boundary_conditions: finite metal nanoparticles with exposed surface facets; finite nanoparticles remain material/surface targets, not isolated molecular chemistry

sources.locator: pp.5–12, workflow and Pd/Pt morphology-reconstruction case studies
sources.evidence_paraphrase: An OpenClaw/GLM-5 agent translates reaction conditions, obtains model parameters and executes MOSP multiscale atomistic morphology reconstruction plus kinetic Monte Carlo. Pd temperature-series structures and Pt pressure/coverage/morphology/activity studies are demonstrated.

aliases: A Chemistry-Grounded Mobile Agent for Working-State Catalyst Simulations
limitations: Its actual physics simulation is sufficient for inclusion although the six-bin scheme only encodes structure reconstruction. KMC does not receive the MD/quantum-dynamics code D, and a prescribed kinetic network does not establish TS/path search R. Energetic parameters are retrieved, not newly calculated by the agent.

name: AutoDFT
demonstrated_target: bulk/surface materials plus standalone CO and H2O optimization/vibration tasks
boundary_conditions: VASP crystal/slab workflows and finite molecular targets represented in plane-wave cells; molecular target identity is distinct from cell periodicity

sources.evidence_paraphrase: A seven-agent VASP framework performs adaptive planning, monitoring and recovery. Its evaluated 34-task table explicitly includes ionic/volume relaxation, SCF/DOS, DFPT phonons and MD, including standalone CO/H2O relaxation and vibration cases alongside crystal and slab tasks.

aliases: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations
limitations: Cross-domain is based on evaluated standalone molecular tasks, not VASP's general support. The system is separately proposed from its VASPBench benchmark and therefore one system, not one system per calculation type. Gaussian portability is an aspiration, not demonstrated evidence.

name: MLIPilot
demonstrated_target: QM7 molecular systems and periodic Cu supercells
boundary_conditions: article explicitly contrasts finite molecular QM7 and periodic Cu EMT datasets

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLMs edit MACE training code and submit experiments whose fixed atomistic evaluation executes energy/force tests, FIRE geometry relaxation and 5,000-step NVE dynamics. Agents accept or revert experiments using returned physical diagnostics on molecular and Cu benchmarks.

aliases: LLM-Driven Auto-Research for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
limitations: The LLM optimizes training rather than directly writing each MD step, but actual simulation feedback determines its choices. Pre-generated QM7 B3LYP labels are not counted as agent-run DFT. Source calls this MLIPilot, distinct from VASPilot.

name: CatDT
demonstrated_target: working heterogeneous catalyst surfaces
boundary_conditions: slab/bulk/facet construction with gas–solid and liquid–solid models

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Builds catalyst surfaces, proposes mechanisms, searches paths/TS and computes kinetics using atomistic tools; liquid–solid capability is not finite-molecule evidence.

name: Paimon
demonstrated_target: LiPF6 liquid electrolytes in DEC/DMC/PC and crystalline solid-electrolyte ion diffusion
boundary_conditions: Liquid cells explicitly require PBC in all three directions (§3.6); crystalline solid-electrolyte MD is separately demonstrated

sources.locator: §§2.1, 2.4–2.5; Fig.4 actual MD runs; Fig.5 solid-electrolyte example; Methods §§3.5–3.6
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Orchestrator/executor agents build electrolyte cells with PACKMOL, relax structures, run LAMMPS equilibration and production, and revise workflows using intermediate feedback. The article distinguishes 30 actual liquid-MD runs from gated tests with precomputed outputs, and separately demonstrates a crystalline solid-electrolyte MD workflow using LLaMP.

aliases: A Robust Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations
limitations: Cross-domain coding follows demonstrated liquid and solid examples, not general software support. Many repeated evaluations replace expensive dynamics with precomputed outputs; actual MD evidence is explicitly limited to the separate full runs and worked example. Transport coefficients are D, not F or electronic E.

name: MDForge
demonstrated_target: SAMPL host–guest binding free energies
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article; explicit/implicit solvent workflow details need separate audit

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM writes and refines MD pipelines with physics feedback on host–guest binding benchmarks.

name: URSA LAMMPS agent
demonstrated_target: metal crystals/liquids, Cu cohesive energy and thermomechanical properties
boundary_conditions: bulk crystal/liquid atomistic models and stacking-fault cells; exact PBC flags not separately audited

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The LLM selects a potential from NIST metadata, authors and runs LAMMPS input, iteratively repairs execution failures, and hands outputs to analysis agents. Benchmarks include cohesive energies, volume curves, thermal expansion, liquid RDF, melting and generalized stacking-fault energy.
The inspected arXiv metadata explicitly gives first submission as 12 June 2026.

aliases: An Agentic Orchestration of Atomistic Simulations
limitations: First date follows source metadata, even though the arXiv identifier begins 2607. Distinct from LAMMPS-Agents (Vriza) and the generic URSA framework. No R mark is assigned to static generalized stacking-fault energies without an explicit path search.

name: AdsMind
demonstrated_target: adsorbate configurations on catalyst slabs
boundary_conditions: cell and periodic boundary conditions explicitly retained in ASE slab reconstruction

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Closed-loop agent uses MLFF relaxation feedback to revise adsorption hypotheses. Main benchmark has Langevin warmup disabled; no MD mark is assigned.

name: LADeQ
demonstrated_target: alkanes C15H32/C20H42, coronene and porphyrin electronic correlation energies
boundary_conditions: finite molecular PySCF CCSD/CISD; STO-3G and single-thread evaluation

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The LLM proposes approximations, edits PySCF CCSD/CISD implementations, and revises them using computed correlation-energy errors, timing and diagnostic logs. The paper reports executed molecular calculations for development and cross-molecule evaluation.

aliases: LLM-Guided Test-Time Discovery of Quantum-Chemical Approximation Algorithms
LLM-guided Automatic approximation Design for Quantum chemistry
limitations: An algorithm-discovery workflow rather than a general researcher-facing QC assistant. Inclusion follows the explicit rule allowing LLM code modification and feedback decisions in executed molecular electronic-structure calculations. Demonstrated conclusions are limited to ground-state correlation energies, four molecules and a minimal basis; no geometry, path or dynamics capabilities are inferred.

name: Agent-MD
demonstrated_target: montmorillonite clay–water desorption
boundary_conditions: explicit periodic boundaries in all three directions

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM reasoning supports campaign construction and event review around deterministic GCMC–MD; production cycles need no live LLM invocation.

limitations: Selective LLM placement is included; counting requires actual planning/modification decisions, not a live LLM at every MD step.

name: CGMas
demonstrated_target: homopolymers and copolymers modeled with paired all-atom and coarse-grained force fields
boundary_conditions: Explicit cubic periodic cells and PBC in x, y and z (Methods §4.3)

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM topology and mapping agents coordinate construction, review and self-correction. Tools build periodic polymer cells, minimize close contacts, execute atomistic annealing/equilibration, derive coarse-grained potentials from the trajectory, and run CG dynamics. PAN and autonomous polymer cases provide executed workflow evidence.

aliases: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics of Polymers
limitations: Human checkpoints are retained in the interactive route. Numerical stages use deterministic tools under LLM orchestration. Density, cooling-scan glass transitions and Boltzmann-inverted potentials do not establish vibrational thermochemistry; F remains blank.

name: Evolving TS workflows
demonstrated_target: TS1X molecular elementary reactions
boundary_conditions: finite molecular endpoint/TS geometries

sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM evolves TS-search code; execution feedback includes Hessian and IRC endpoint checks. The LLM optimizes the workflow rather than directly making every reaction decision.

name: ARCHE
demonstrated_target: organic/organometallic molecular mechanisms
boundary_conditions: finite molecular asymmetric, radical and Ni-catalysis examples

sources.locator: Abstract; SI TSPipeline/C.10 independently checked by parent researcher
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Closed-loop mechanistic hypotheses are checked computationally across stereocontrol, radical cleavage and Ni-catalyzed selectivity examples.

limitations: Full PDF exceeds web-reader size limit; main inclusion/object/task claims use the abstract. Parent independently inspected SI mapping/force-field/TS and frequency/IRC/endpoint chain. Do not infer absent geometric or scientific validation capabilities.

name: Multireference QC agent
demonstrated_target: QUEST molecular excited states and transition-metal complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular ORCA calculations

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Selects active spaces, submits ORCA calculations, recovers convergence and identifies electronic states; evaluation covers molecular vertical transition energies.

name: SQD-Agent
demonstrated_target: small-molecule ground-state energies including N2 and CH2O
boundary_conditions: finite molecular electronic Hamiltonians

sources.locator: Section I Figs. 1–5; Section II Discussions and Future Scope
sources.evidence_paraphrase: An LLM orchestration layer generates and executes molecular SQD electronic-structure workflows on classical simulators and a quantum processor, with explicit human confirmation before hardware submission.

limitations: Proof of concept in a minimal basis; the authors explicitly describe human-supervised reconfiguration and no autonomous closed feedback loop. Inclusion does not imply full autonomy or quantum advantage.

name: MLP Copilot
demonstrated_target: bare and oxide-shell aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
boundary_conditions: finite nanoparticles in a reactive simulation environment; atomistic materials target regardless of box periodicity

sources.locator: §1.1; Methods §3.3 Human-Audited Multiagent Framework; MovieS1 description
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Language-model agents organize evidence, assist validation planning and prepare decisions in an executed active-learning MLP campaign, including CP2K energy/force labeling, model evaluation and ANP oxidation MD. Scientific acceptance and deployment remain human controlled.

sources.locator: README/Simulation Data And DigAuto; Start With Initial Data
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Official project links the earlier Auto-MLP campaign, retained nanoparticle MD trajectories and energy/force data, and tools/skills for dataset planning and potential evaluation.

aliases: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the oxide gatekeeper in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
limitations: Human-audited planning/validation assistance qualifies under the broad inclusion rule; do not describe it as an autonomous MD scientist or claim the LLM directly made every execution decision. October15 is the inspected online publication date, not a verified first software release. Auto-MLP and the current runtime are treated as one campaign family to avoid duplicate counting.

name: Magnolia
demonstrated_target: aromatic molecules, gas-phase butane and modified DNA
boundary_conditions: finite molecular QC/gas-phase dynamics and solvated DNA cells

sources.evidence_paraphrase: The agent generates and optimizes aromatic structures, evaluates electronic properties, runs butane dynamics and a relaxed torsion scan, and constructs and tracks modified-DNA MD campaigns.

limitations: Human-reviewed memory and scientific decisions remain explicit. A torsional scan is not coded as a TS/IRC proof. Docking claims and proprietary targets do not determine task marks.
